newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP to recommend Japan interest raise rise--NHK.
newsitem.headline: LDP to recommend Japan interest raise rise--NHK.

text.p: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) will make a recommendation to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto by the end of this month that Japan raise its official discount rate, NHK television reported on Tuesday.
NHK said an LDP committee studying administrative reforms will make the recommendation in light of last week's change in Japan's foreign exchange laws.
It did not say what the extent of the rate rise recommended by the LDP would be.

On May 16, parliament formally approved changes to the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law aimed at revitalising Tokyo markets by scrapping a rule limiting foreign exchange business to authorised banks and enabling freer cross-border capital transactions.
LDP officials were not immediately available to confirm the NHK report.
The Bank of Japan cut the discount rate to a record low 0.5 percent on September 8, 1995.
